questions.question: Which set of items must be compatible before an online model decision is trustworthy?
options: Request schema, feature values, preprocessing, artifact, and decision policy
Only the container image and GPU type
Only the model weights and HTTP status code
Only the training notebook and dashboard
questions.explanation: A production prediction is a contract across the request, features, transformations, model, and policy. A mismatch can produce a fast but incorrect decision.

questions.question: At 1M requests per second, how much traffic does a 5% canary receive?
options: 500 requests per second
5,000 requests per second
50,000 requests per second
500,000 requests per second
questions.explanation: One million multiplied by 0.05 is 50,000 requests per second. Canary traffic can still be a substantial production workload.

questions.question: What does point-in-time feature construction prevent?
options: Training on values that were not available when the historical decision occurred
Model artifact signing
Serving requests from more than one region
Collecting delayed outcome labels
questions.explanation: Point-in-time joins prevent future information from leaking into training and evaluation, keeping offline evidence comparable to online conditions.

questions.question: A candidate improves overall offline AUC but breaches a protected-slice regression limit. What should the release system do?
options: Promote because the aggregate metric improved
Skip the slice metric after the canary starts
Hold or reject the candidate until the agreed slice gate passes
Increase cache capacity to compensate
questions.explanation: Release gates include absolute and slice-level bounds. An aggregate improvement does not make a material slice regression acceptable.

questions.question: Why should feature-cache misses have bounded concurrency?
options: To prevent a cache outage or hot key from overwhelming the authoritative feature store
To ensure every request retrains the model
To remove version information from the cache key
To make monitoring asynchronous
questions.explanation: Coalescing misses and capping fallback work stop a degraded cache from transferring unbounded demand to the authoritative store.

questions.question: Which observation should freeze promotion even when service latency and error rate are healthy?
options: A versioned drift or delayed-outcome quality regression
A successful container health check
Stable CPU utilization
A completed artifact upload
questions.explanation: Infrastructure health does not prove model behavior is healthy. Drift and outcome quality are model-specific signals that must control rollout.
